projects.title: Featured Projects
projects.movieTicketBookingDescription: The web-based Movie Ticket Booking System using Yii2 (PHP), enables users to browse movies, check seat availability, and book tickets online, with admin functionality for managing theaters, movies, and reservations.
projects.movieFinderDescription: The Movie Finder App integrates the TMDB API to enable movie searches, display trending titles, and detailed movie information while tracking user search activity.
projects.allergyAppDescription: This app provides a straightforward answer to the amount of allergy medication that is required for a day. It integrates data from the Ambee and OpenWeatherMap APIs to accurately calculate daily pollen concentration levels and temperature.
projects.millionaireTitle: Who Wants to Be a Millionaire
projects.millionaireDescription: A desktop version of the popular quiz game, developed using C++ and the Qt framework. It features a dynamic UI.
projects.ecommerceCppDescription: This C++ program simulates an e-commerce system where customers can browse products, view details, and make purchases. It manages budgets, updates stock quantities, and saves purchase data to text files. Users can search products by name or manufacturer.
projects.transformersAppDescription: A lightweight translation playground using Transformers.js and the Xenova NLLB model. Supports over 200 languages and runs entirely in the browser with no API or backend calls. Built with Vite and uses Web Workers for smooth UI performance, with real-time progress indicators during model loading.
projects.sentimentAnalyzerDescription: Lightweight React app performing real-time sentiment analysis in the browser using Transformers.js. Uses a Web Worker to run the distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english model without blocking the UI. Features client-side inference (no server), Hugging Face-powered.
projects.objectDetectorDescription: A React-based web app for real-time object detection using Transformers.js and the DETR ResNet-50 model. Runs entirely in the browser (client-side inference) without any backend/API calls. Upload an image to detect objects and draw bounding boxes using JavaScript and WebAssembly.
